title: OpenAI compatibility: event-proxy + toolcall contextualizer
creator: Maya Gupta
description: Implement an OpenAI Chat Completions compatibility proxy that preserves streaming semantics, function/tool call signals, and structured-output envelopes while emitting a consistent event protocol for downstream observability and sidecar routers. Focus on request shaping, partial-stream idempotency, and lossless toolcall context propagation between Redwood runtime and legacy OpenAI client expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts standard OpenAI ChatCompletions request shapes and returns compatible streaming SSE frames (data: [DONE] style) for legacy clients
Function/tool call intents are surfaced as discrete events during streaming and replay as single function invocation payloads in final response
Ordered streaming chunks preserve idempotency across retries and reconnections using a deterministic fragment id scheme
Structured output (JSON-LD / annotated blocks) is mapped to Redwood structured-output API and back to OpenAI-compatible text/choices payload without semantic loss
Telemetry events include request_id, fragment_id, toolcall_id, latency_ms, and chosen_model_variant; events are consumable by console rollup dashboards
End-to-end test harness validating stream reconnection, partial resume, and toolcall replay is added to runtime CI
decision_log: 2025-02-21: Chose event-proxy pattern over heavy adapter in runtime to minimize per-request CPU overhead and centralize compatibility mapping
2025-02-24: Use stable UUID v1 for request_id (time-ordered) and a 64-bit monotonic fragment counter for fragment_id to maintain ordering guarantees
2025-02-26: Encode toolcall context as base64-encoded JSON blob in streaming event to avoid breaking legacy SSE parsers; runtime will store normalized toolcall metadata separately for observability

2025-02-28: Opted to support two mapping modes: transparent-pass (for customers that want raw Redwood responses) and emulation-mode (for legacy OpenAI clients). Default to emulation-mode for hosted endpoints behind OA-compat route
technical_notes: Mapping inbound messages: map OpenAI message.role -> Redwood role + extra metadata mapping for system/instruction tokens

Streaming behavior: interleave 'toolcall_start', 'toolcall_chunk', 'toolcall_end' events into SSE stream; ensure finalized function call appears as a single 'choices' object in final non-stream response
Idempotency: assign fragment_id per outgoing chunk and store ack state in short-lived KV cache to support reconnect resume within a 30s window
Backpressure: implement token-window advisory header for legacy clients to signal allowed burst tokens; runtime will throttle accordingly

Structured outputs: when Redwood returns structured-output blocks, serialize to both 'content' and 'delta' with a metadata wrapper to allow legacy clients to parse as plain text while preserving machine-readable payloads for Redwood console
Telemetry: emit lightweight events to event bus (kafka) with schema version header. Event names: compat.request.start, compat.stream.chunk, compat.toolcall.invoke, compat.request.end
Security: strip or redact customer-provided tool metadata when emitting unencrypted events unless customer opt-in for observability is set
Performance target: additional CPU < 5% p99 overhead on high-throughput endpoints; added memory for fragment metadata capped at 256KB per request
